title: engagement-sprint-canvas-and-decision-log
content:
ENGAGEMENT SPRINT CANVAS + DECISION LOG
Owner: Asha Patel (solutions-engineering)
Stakeholders: Customer (ACME Retail) - Product + Infra leads; Redwood: Solutions Eng, Platform Eng, SRE
Purpose: Run a 6-week evaluation that validates latency/throughput under ACME transaction patterns, verifies private deployment networking, and produces a deployment proposal with acceptance criteria for Dedicated capacity.

Scope (in-scope):
- Hosted API and Dedicated-capacity smoke tests (small traffic profile)
- Private deployment (VPC peering) basic connectivity and auth validation
- End-to-end latency and tail-latency measurements for typical request shapes (chat + retrieval + single-turn generation)
- Cost/throughput projection using Redwood Optimize suggestions
- Workshop with ACME product + infra to align rollout plan

Out of scope (for this sprint):
- Full on-prem air-gapped installation
- Model training/finetuning
- Deep security audit beyond standard KMS/HSM verification (will be a follow-up)

Success hypotheses / acceptance criteria (customer-facing):
1) 95th percentile latency <= 250ms for small single-turn text generation under their peak concurrency of 80 QPS (within Dedicated slot sizing).
2) End-to-end integration with ACME auth flow (OIDC) completed and verified in VPC environment (smoke requests succeed).
3) Cost estimate for productioning 100M tokens/month <= customer budget threshold (provided in kickoff) and validated by Redwood Optimize baseline.
4) Runbook and rollback plan delivered and reviewed by ACME SRE.

Milestones & 6-week timeline (high-level)
Week 0 (pre-work, 3 business days): Kickoff, data share checklist, environment access, baseline measurement plan.
Week 1: Hosted API tests; synthetic load + trace collection; initial latency profile; quick workshop 60m to align metrics.
Week 2: Deploy Dedicated test pool; run throughput tests; measure autoscale behavior; identify kernel/quantization settings to try.
Week 3: Private VPC trial environment (connectivity + auth); run integration tests and collect logs; security checklist items.
Week 4: Mixed workload day (retrieval + chat + reranking) with prefix caching enabled; measure end-to-end tail latency; cost simulation.
Week 5: Failure injection & resilience testing (region failover, model fallback); finalize cost-performance tradeoffs.
Week 6: Deliverables: runbook, decision log, deployment proposal, exec summary and next-step contract ask.

Sprint Canvas (roles & primary owners):
- SE Lead: Asha Patel — overall project management, customer sync, acceptance criteria sign-off
- Platform Eng support: Liam Chen — Dedicated pool config, autoscaling policies, kernel selection
- SRE liaison: Nora Williams — private network validation, observability hooks, runbook review
- Product / Solutions SME: Devon Singh — eval metrics, quality thresholds, prompt regression checks
- Customer PM: ACME - Priya Shah — scope approvals, internal test fixtures

Key deliverables (week-aligned):
- Week 1: baseline latency report (artifact: hosted-baseline-2025-10-31.log), prompt set v1
- Week 2: dedicated-config.yml, throughput-report.csv, cost-sim-1.xlsx
- Week 3: vpc-connect-checklist.md, oidc-smoke-run.log
- Week 4: mixed-workload-report.pdf, caching-config.json
- Week 5: resilience-runbook.md, failure-inject-results.log
- Week 6: final-proposal.pdf, runbook-for-acme.md, exec-summary-slide-deck.pdf

Decision Log (live):
- [2025-10-29] Decide to start with quantized 4-bit variant for the retrieval model to reduce memory pressure on Dedicated pool. Owner: Liam. Rationale: expected 2x throughput increase with minimal quality loss per internal eval.
- [2025-11-03] Agree to use OIDC passthrough (customer-managed) for initial private tests instead of full KMS integration. Owner: Nora. Rationale: reduces setup time for POC and satisfies smoke-test objectives; long-term security integration will be separate.
- [2025-11-06] Swap autoscale policy from CPU-based trigger to request-latency-based trigger after seeing tail-latency spikes in week 2 tests. Owner: Liam. Rationale: better aligns with customer SLOs.

Risk register (prioritized):
1) Network access delays / VPN/VPC peer tickets — Mitigation: pre-kickoff checklist for firewall rules and shared test VM; contingency: use hosted API results to validate performance assumptions.
2) Model quality regression when applying aggressive quantization — Mitigation: maintain prompt/regression suite and rollback to higher-precision variant; contingency: increase Dedicated capacity or enable CPU fallback.
3) Overrun on customer infra calendar (access windows) — Mitigation: schedule windows early and agree on alternate test plan that runs synthetic traffic from Redwood.
4) Cost projection mismatch — Mitigation: run Optimize profiles with conservative margins and log assumptions in proposal.

Workshop notes (initial 60m align, 2025-10-30):
Attendees: Asha, Liam, Nora, Devon, Priya (ACME), Tom (ACME infra)
Outputs:
- Agreed canonical request shapes: chat-short (<=128 tokens), retrieval+rerank (embedding + 3 candidate rerank), bulk-embed (batch size 32)
- Customer provided sample traffic trace (anonymized) and a 48-hour snapshot for baseline generation
- Decided to use Redwood Optimize baseline run to estimate Dedicated slot sizing (customer wants +/- 15% accuracy)

Testing checklist (run for each major test):
- Preconditions: credentials validated, metrics ingestion (Datadog) wired, alerting Slack integration confirmed
- Load profile defined and agreed (QPS, concurrency, payload size distribution)
- Latency buckets instrumented (p50, p90, p95, p99), token counts logged
- Cost simulator run with raw token counts and selected batching settings
- Regression suite (prompt_sanity_v1) run before/after config changes

Customer handover & next steps (post-week 6):
- Draft Dedicated sizing contract (options: baseline, baseline+burst, baseline+autoscale) — owner: Asha & Sales Eng
- Schedule 2-hour deployment workshop for production cutover (owner: Nora)
- Handoff checklist for Customer Success: runbook, SLA doc, billing forecast, escalation contacts

Open questions (to resolve before end of week 2):
- Does ACME require request/response payload encryption beyond TLS at transit (customer to confirm)
- Confirm internal tagging strategy for cost attribution (who owns tags)
- Agree on post-POC KPIs and minimum viable production SLOs

Notes-to-self / quick actions: 
- Asha: prepare prompt set v2 with company-style examples by 2025-11-02
- Liam: run quantization sensitivity test on retrieval model and upload results to linked_artifacts by 2025-11-04
- Nora: draft VPC checklist and share with Tom (ACME) by 2025-11-05

Appendix: quick glance metrics to track during POC (summary table)
- Throughput target: 80 QPS peak (small-gen), 5K embeds/min for bulk-embed windows
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms small-gen, p99 <= 500ms retrieval pipeline
- Cost target: <= $X per 1M tokens (detailed in cost-sim-1.xlsx)

End of document.
